- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment values) — reduce forecast peaks when sentiment is strong.
- Underestimate prices after sharp declines or negative sentiment spikes — adjust downward bias when sentiment turns negative.
- Overshoot after recent price spikes — cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below prior high or adjust based on sentiment momentum.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 5–10 day average, reduce by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was positive 3–5 days prior, reduce forecast by 2–5% to account for delayed market reaction.
- Avoid overconfidence in short-term momentum — if sentiment is rising but price is falling, reduce forecast slope to avoid “over-leveraged” optimism.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, reduce forecast by 3–5% if sentiment is negative or mixed over last 7 days — price tends to revert faster under uncertainty.
